sg_grid_groups.uniqueName: group/Used by NetApp DII data collection
sg_grid_groups.groupURN: urn:sgws:identity::0:group/Used by NetApp DII data collection

annotations.description: Storage Node with ADC service is offline. Expansion and decommission operations are blocked until ADC quorum is restored.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Determine if there is another alert affecting this node. This alert might be resolved when you resolve the other alert.
2. Go to the Nodes page to verify that all Storage Nodes are online. Power on any nodes that are offline.
3. If the issue persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The nodes that run the Cassandra service are having trouble communicating with each other.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert indicates that something is interfering with node-to-node communications. There might be a network issue or the Cassandra service might be down on one or more Storage Nodes.
1. Go to the Nodes page to verify that all Storage Nodes are online.
2. If other alerts are active, investigate and resolve them first.
3. If the issue persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The Cassandra compaction process is overloaded.
annotations.recommendedActions:
If the compaction process is overloaded, read performance might be degraded and RAM might be used up. The Cassandra service might also become unresponsive or crash.
1. Restart the Cassandra service by following the steps for restarting a service in the grid node maintenance procedures.
2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: Cassandra has detected table corruption.  Cassandra automatically restarts if it detects table corruption.
annotations.recommendedActions: Contact technical support.

annotations.description: The progress of Cassandra database repairs is slow.
annotations.recommendedActions:
When database repairs are slow, Cassandra data consistency operations are impeded. If this condition persists for more than 48 hours, client queries, such as bucket listings, might show deleted data.
1. Confirm that all Storage Nodes are online and there are no networking-related alerts.
2. Monitor this alert for up to 2 days to see if the issue resolves on its own.
3. If database repairs continue to proceed slowly, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The Cassandra repair service is not available.
annotations.recommendedActions:
The Cassandra repair service exists on all Storage Nodes and provides critical repair functions for the Cassandra database. If this condition persists for more than 48 hours, client queries, such as bucket listings, might show deleted data.
1. Go to the Nodes page to verify that all Storage Nodes are online.
2. If other alerts are active, investigate and resolve them first.
3. If the issue persists, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: Cassandra repair metrics out of date

annotations.description: The metrics that describe Cassandra repair jobs are out of date.
annotations.recommendedActions:
If this condition persists for more than 48 hours, client queries, such as bucket listings, might show deleted data.

1. Reboot the node. From the Grid Manager, go to Nodes, select the node, and select the Tasks tab.
2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The Cassandra auto-compactor has experienced an error.
annotations.recommendedActions:
The Cassandra auto-compactor exists on all Storage Nodes and manages the size of the Cassandra database for overwrite and delete heavy workloads. While this condition persists, certain workloads will experience unexpectedly high metadata consumption.

1. Determine if there is another alert affecting this node. This alert might be resolved when you resolve the other alert.
2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: An internal StorageGRID process sent a write request to Cassandra that was too large.
annotations.recommendedActions: Contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: Cassandra auto-compactor metrics out of date

annotations.description: The metrics that describe the Cassandra auto-compactor are out of date.
annotations.recommendedActions:
The Cassandra auto-compactor exists on all Storage Nodes and manages the size of the Cassandra database for overwrite and delete heavy workloads. While this condition persists, certain workloads will experience unexpectedly high metadata consumption.

1. Determine if there is another alert affecting this node. This alert might be resolved when you resolve the other alert.
2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The health check for Cloud Storage Pools detected one or more new errors.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1.  Go to the Cloud Storage Pools section of the ILM > Storage Pools page.
2.  Look at the Last Error column to determine which Cloud Storage Pool has an error.
3.  See the instructions for managing objects with ILM.

annotations.description: When debug mode is enabled, system performance might be negatively impacted.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to the Grid Manager > API Documentation > Go to private API documentation > log-levels.
2. Use POST /private/log-levels/restore-default to restore the default log level configuration.
3. The alert might take up to 15 minutes to clear. If the alert persists, contact technical support.
annotations.services: {{ with printf "group by (job) (storagegrid_private_ade_debug_level{instance='%s'} != -1 OR storagegrid_private_log_level{instance='%s'} != 6)" $labels.instance $labels.instance | query }}{{ range $index, $element := . }}{{if $index}}, {{end}}{{ $element.Labels.job }}{{end}}{{end}}

annotations.description: The DHCP lease on a network interface has expired.
annotations.recommendedActions:
If the DHCP lease has expired, follow the recommended actions:

1. Ensure there is connectivity between this node and the DHCP server on the affected interface.
2. Ensure there are IP addresses available to assign in the affected subnet on the DHCP server.
3. Ensure there is a permanent reservation for the IP address configured in the DHCP server. Or, use the StorageGRID Change IP tool to assign a static IP address outside of the DHCP address pool. See the instructions in the network maintenance procedures.

annotations.description: The DHCP lease on a network interface is expiring soon.
annotations.recommendedActions:
To prevent the DHCP lease from expiring, follow the recommended actions:

1. Ensure there is connectivity between this node and the DHCP server on the affected interface.
2. Ensure there are IP addresses available to assign in the affected subnet on the DHCP server.
3. Ensure there is a permanent reservation for the IP address configured in the DHCP server. Or, use the StorageGRID Change IP tool to assign a static IP address outside of the DHCP address pool. See the instructions in the network maintenance procedures.
annotations.dhcpLeaseTimeRemainingPercent: {{ printf `(storagegrid_private_dhcp_expiry_timestamp{instance="%s", device="%s"} - time()) / storagegrid_private_dhcp_lease_time` $labels.instance $labels.device | query | first | value }}

annotations.description: The DHCP server is unavailable.
annotations.recommendedActions:
The StorageGRID node is unable to contact your DHCP server. The DHCP lease for the node's IP address cannot be validated.

1. Ensure there is connectivity between this node and the DHCP server on the affected interface.
2. Ensure there are IP addresses available to assign in the affected subnet on the DHCP server.
3. Ensure there is a permanent reservation for the IP address configured in the DHCP server. Or, use the StorageGRID Change IP tool to assign a static IP address outside of the DHCP address pool. See the instructions in the network maintenance procedures.

annotations.description: The StorageGRID node has been unable to resolve domain names.
annotations.recommendedActions:
The StorageGRID node is unable to resolve domain names.

1. Ensure the DNS server is correctly configured and reachable from the StorageGRID node.
2. Run "nslookup" on the node to manually check domain name resolution. Ensure the domain name is resolved.
3. Restart the service by following the steps for restarting a service in the grid node maintenance procedures.

annotations.description: Erasure-coded fragments can no longer be verified. Corrupt fragments might not be repaired.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Address any issues affecting the Storage Node's filesystem or file operations.
2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The EC rebalance procedure has failed or has been stopped.
annotations.recommendedActions:
The job to rebalance erasure-coded data among Storage Nodes has failed or has been paused by the user.

1. Ensure that all Storage Nodes at the site being rebalanced are online and available.
2. Ensure that there are no volume failures at the site being rebalanced. If there are, terminate the EC rebalance job so that you can run a repair job.

  'rebalance-data terminate --job-id <ID>'

3. Ensure that there are no service failures on the site being rebalanced. If a service is not running, follow the steps for starting or restarting a service in the recovery and maintenance instructions.
4. After resolving any issues, restart the job by running the following command on the primary Admin Node:

  'rebalance-data start --job-id <ID>'

5. If you are unable to resolve the problem, contact technical support.

annotations.description: A repair job for EC data has failed or has been stopped.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Ensure that there are sufficient available Storage Nodes or volumes to take the place of the failed Storage Node or volume.
2. Ensure that there are sufficient available Storage Nodes to satisfy the active ILM policy.
3. Ensure there are no network connectivity issues.
4. After resolving any issues, restart the job by running the following command on the primary Admin Node:

  'repair-data start-ec-node-repair --repair-id <ID>'

5. If you are unable to resolve the problem, contact technical support.

annotations.description: A repair job for EC data has stalled.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Ensure that there are sufficient available Storage Nodes or volumes to take the place of the failed Storage Node or volume.
2. Ensure there are no network connectivity issues.
3. After resolving any issues, check if the alert is resolved. To see a more detailed report on the repair progress, run the following command on the primary Admin Node:

  'repair-data show-ec-repair-status --repair-id <ID>'

4. If you are unable to resolve the problem, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The email notification for an alert could not be sent.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert is triggered when an alert email notification fails or a test email (sent from the Alerts > Email Setup page) cannot be delivered.
1. Sign in to Grid Manager from the Admin Node listed in the Site/Node column of the alert.
2. Go to the Alerts > Email Setup page, check the settings, and change them if required.
3. Click Send Test Email, and check the inbox of a test recipient for the email. A new instance of this alert might be triggered if the test email cannot be sent.
4. If the test email could not be sent, confirm your email server is online.
5. If the server is working, go to Support > Tools > Logs, and collect the log for the Admin Node. Specify a time period that is 15 minutes before and after the time of the alert.
6. Extract the downloaded archive, and review the contents of prometheus.log (/GID<gid>_<time_stamp>/<site_node>/<time_stamp>/metrics/prometheus.log).
7. If you are unable to resolve the problem, contact technical support.

annotations.description: Failed to apply firewall configuration.
annotations.recommendedActions:
Security protections from the node firewall could not be applied.
1. Reboot the impacted node. From the Grid Manager, go to Nodes, select the node, and select the Tasks tab.
2. If the alert persists, go to Support > Tools > Logs, and collect the Application Logs for the impacted node. Specify a time period that is 15 minutes before and after the time of the alert.
3. Extract the downloaded archive, and review the contents of initSG.log and node log (/GID<gid>_<time_stamp>/<site_node>/<time_stamp>/install/initSG.sh and /GID<gid>_<time_stamp>/<site_node>/<time_stamp>/base-os-logs/var/log/storagegrid/nodes/<node_name>.log).
4. If you are unable to resolve the problem, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: IAM Roles Anywhere end-entity certification expiration

annotations.description: IAM Roles Anywhere end-entity certificate is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to the Cloud Storage Pools section of the ILM > Storage Pools page.
2. Select the endpoint that has a IAM Roles Anywhere end-entity certificate that will expire soon.
3. Select Edit endpoint to upload a new certificate.

annotations.description: A placement instruction in an ILM rule cannot be achieved for certain objects.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert indicates that a node required by a placement instruction is unavailable or that an ILM rule is misconfigured. For example, a rule might specify more replicated copies than there are Storage Nodes.
1. Ensure that all nodes are online.
2. If all nodes are online, review the placement instructions in all ILM rules that are used in the active ILM policy. Confirm there are valid instructions for all objects. See the instructions for managing objects with ILM.
3. As required, update rule settings and activate a new policy.
Note: It might take up to 1 day for the alert to clear.
4. Ensure that there are enough writable Storage Nodes to meet the ILM policy. Consider Storage Node expansion if the policy requires additional Storage Nodes. See the instructions for managing storage nodes in ILM policies that use erasure-coding schemes.
5. If the problem persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The grid federation connection between the local and remote grid is not working.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Review the settings on the Grid Federation page for both the local and the remote grids. Confirm that all values are correct. See "Manage grid federation connections" in the instructions for administering StorageGRID.
2. Review the certificates used for the connection. Make sure that certificates have not expired and that the details are valid.
3. Confirm that all Admin and Gateway Nodes in the local and remote grids are online and available. Resolve any alerts that might be affecting these nodes and try again.
4. If you provided a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the local or remote grid, confirm the DNS server is online and available.

annotations.description: Unable to synchronize federated groups and users from the identity source.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1.  Confirm that the configured LDAP server is online and available.
2.  Review the settings on the Identity Federation page. Confirm that all values are current. See "Configuring a federated identity source" in the instructions for administering StorageGRID.
3.  Click Test Connection to validate the settings for the LDAP server.
4.  If you cannot resolve the issue, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: Identity federation synchronization failure for a tenant

annotations.description: Unable to synchronize federated groups and users from the identity source configured by a tenant.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1.  Sign in to the Tenant Manager.
2.  Confirm that the LDAP server configured by the tenant is online and available.
3.  Review the settings on the Identity Federation page. Confirm that all values are current. See "Configuring a federated identity source" in the instructions for using a tenant account.
4.  Click Test Connection to validate the settings for the LDAP server.
5.  If you cannot resolve the issue, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The ILM scan rate is set to less than 100 objects/second.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert indicates that someone has changed the ILM scan rate for your system to less than 100 objects/second (default: 400 objects/second). The active ILM policy might not be applied to newly ingested objects. Subsequent changes to the ILM policy will not be applied to existing objects.

1. Determine if a temporary change was made to the ILM scan rate as part of an ongoing support investigation.
2. Contact technical support.

Attention: Never change the ILM scan rate without contacting technical support.

annotations.description: The certificate authority (CA) certificate used to sign the key management server (KMS) certificate is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Using the KMS software, update the CA certificate for the key management server.
2. From the Grid Manager, go to Configuration > Key Management Server.
3. Select the KMS that has a certificate status warning.
4. Select Edit.
5. Select Next to go to Step 2 (Upload Server Certificate).
6. Select Browse to upload the new certificate.
7. Select Save.

annotations.description: The client certificate for a key management server is about to expire
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to Configuration > Key Management Server.
2. Select the KMS that has a certificate status warning.
3. Select Edit.
4. Select Next to go to Step 3 (Upload Client Certificates).
5. Select Browse to upload the new certificate.
6. Select Browse to upload the new private key.
7. Select Save.

annotations.description: The configuration for the key management server exists but failed to load.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Determine if there is another alert affecting this node. This alert might be resolved when you resolve the other alert.
2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: An appliance node could not connect to the key management server for its site.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to the Key Management Server page.
2. Confirm that the port and hostname entries are correct.
3. Confirm that the server certificate, client certificate, and the client certificate private key are correct and not expired.
4. Ensure that firewall settings allow the appliance node to communicate with the specified KMS.
5. Correct any networking or DNS issues.
6. If you need assistance or this alert persists, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: KMS key failed to decrypt an appliance volume

annotations.description: One or more volumes on an appliance with node encryption enabled could not be decrypted with the current KMS key.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Determine if there is another alert affecting this node. This alert might be resolved when you resolve the other alert.
2. Ensure that the key management server (KMS) has the configured encryption key and any previous key versions.
3. If you need assistance or this alert persists, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: KMS encryption key name not found

annotations.description: The configured key management server does not have an encryption key that matches the name provided.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Confirm that the KMS assigned to the site is using the correct name for the encryption key and any prior versions.
2. If you need assistance or this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: All appliance volumes were successfully decrypted, but one or more volumes could not rotate to the latest key.
annotations.recommendedActions: Contact technical support.

annotations.description: No key management server exists for this site.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to the Key Management Server page.
2. Add a KMS for this site or add a default KMS.
See the instructions for administering StorageGRID.

annotations.description: The server certificate used by the key management server (KMS) is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Using the KMS software, update the server certificate for the key management server.
2. If you need assistance or this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: An appliance node could not connect to one or more servers in the key management server cluster for its site.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to the Key Management Server page and select the KMS name.
2. Confirm that each of the servers listed in Hostname is online.
3. Ensure that firewall settings allow the appliance node to communicate with each node.
4. Correct any networking, certificate or DNS issues.
5. If you need assistance or this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The disk queue for audit messages is full. If this condition is not addressed, S3 operations might fail.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Check the audit load on the system. If there have been a significant number of transactions, the alert should resolve itself over time, and you can ignore the alert.
2. If the alert persists and increases in severity, view a chart of the queue size. If the number is steadily increasing over hours or days, the audit load has likely exceeded the audit capacity of the system.
3. Reduce the client operation rate or decrease the number of audit messages logged by changing the audit level for Client Writes and Client Reads to Error or Off (Configuration > Monitoring > Audit).

sg_alert_rules.name: ListBucket permission check for Get/Head object disabled

annotations.description: ListBucket permission check for GetObject/HeadObject on non-existent keys is disabled.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. By default, the ListBucket permission check for GetObject and HeadObject requests is enabled. When disabled, the s3:ListBucket permission isn't checked for GetObject and HeadObject requests if the requested key doesn't exist. This alert indicates that the permission check is disabled.
2. This setting is deprecated and will be removed in version 12.2. After you upgrade to version 12.2, the ListBucket permission check will always be enforced.
3. Contact technical support to enable the permission check before a software upgrade.

expressions.minor: (sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_leak_handler_leaked_object_chunks_bytes) - sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_leak_handler_leaked_object_chunks_cleanup_bytes{result="success"})) / sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_storage_volume_total_space) * 100 > 1
expressions.major: (sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_leak_handler_leaked_object_chunks_bytes) - sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_leak_handler_leaked_object_chunks_cleanup_bytes{result="success"})) / sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_storage_volume_total_space) * 100 > 5
expressions.critical: (sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_leak_handler_leaked_object_chunks_bytes) - sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_leak_handler_leaked_object_chunks_cleanup_bytes{result="success"})) / sum by (instance, node_id, site_name, site_id) (storagegrid_storage_volume_total_space) * 100 > 10

annotations.description: Orphan objects have been detected.
annotations.recommendedActions: Contact technical support.

annotations.description: The space available for audit logs is low. If this condition is not addressed, S3 operations might fail.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to the Alerts page. Monitor this alert to see if the issue resolves on its own and the disk space becomes available again.
2. Contact technical support if the available space continues to decrease.
annotations.total: {{ with printf "node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance='%s', mountpoint='/var/local/audit/export'}" $labels.instance | query }} {{ . | first | value }} {{end}}

sg_alert_rules.name: Management interface endpoints in fallback mode

annotations.description: All management interface endpoints have been falling back to the default ports for too long.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert is triggered when management interface endpoints have been falling back to the system-default ports (443, 8443, and 9443) for more than 24 hours. This condition can occur if technical support runs a CLI script to start fallback mode, but doesn't run a script to exit fallback mode.
1. From the Grid Manager, go to Configuration, select Load balancer endpoints.
2. Select the Management interface tab.
3. Review the list of management interface endpoints. Optionally, remove any endpoints you aren't using or create any new endpoints you need.
4. Contact technical support to exit fallback mode.

annotations.description: A high percentage of Java heap space is being used.
annotations.recommendedActions:
If the Java heap becomes full, metadata services can become unavailable and client requests can fail.

1. Review the ILM activity on the Dashboard. This alert might resolve on its own when the ILM workload decreases.
2. Determine if there is another alert affecting this node. This alert might be resolved when you resolve the other alert.
3. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The average time for Cassandra metadata queries is too long.
annotations.recommendedActions:
An increase in query latency can be caused by a hardware change, such as replacing a disk; a workload change, such as a sudden increase in ingests; or a network change, such as a communication problem between nodes and sites.

1.  Determine if there were any hardware, workload, or network changes around the time the query latency increased.
2.  If you are unable to resolve the problem, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The offset between local clock and Network Time Protocol (NTP) time is too large.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1.  Reboot the node. From the Grid Manager, go to Nodes, select the node, and select the Tasks tab.
2.  Check that all NTP servers are operating normally.
3.  Ensure that no external service is changing the clock time, for example a Hypervisor or CronJob.

annotations.description: The space available for storing object metadata is low.
annotations.recommendedActions:
You must add new Storage Nodes in an expansion procedure. See "Troubleshooting Low metadata storage alerts" in the instructions for monitoring and troubleshooting StorageGRID. Also see the instructions for expanding your grid.

Critical alert:

  1.  Stop ingesting objects.

  2.  Add Storage Nodes immediately.


Major alert:

  Add Storage Nodes immediately.


Minor alert:

  1.  Monitor the rate at which object metadata space is being used. Select Nodes > Storage Node > Storage, and view the Storage Used - Object Metadata graph.

  2.  Add Storage Nodes as soon as possible.

annotations.description: The space available for the metrics database is low.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to the Alerts page. Monitor this alert to see if the issue resolves on its own and the disk space becomes available again.
2. Contact technical support if the available space continues to decrease.
annotations.total: {{ with printf "node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance='%s', mountpoint='/var/local/mysql_ibdata'}" $labels.instance | query }} {{ . | first | value }} {{end}}

annotations.description: The space available for storing object data is low.
annotations.recommendedActions: Perform an expansion procedure. You can add new Storage Nodes or add storage volumes (LUNs) to existing Storage Nodes. See the instructions for expanding a StorageGRID system. If your grid is nearly full, see the instructions for planning a StorageGRID expansion.

annotations.description: The storage volume soft read-only watermark override is less than the minimum optimized watermark for a Storage Node.
annotations.recommendedActions: To learn how to resolve this alert, go to the StorageGRID doc site and search for "troubleshoot low read-only watermark override alerts".

annotations.description: The space available on the root disk is low.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to the Alerts page. Monitor this alert to see if the issue resolves on its own and the disk space becomes available again.
2. Contact technical support if the available space continues to decrease.
annotations.total: {{ with printf "node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance='%s', mountpoint='/'}" $labels.instance | query }} {{ . | first | value }} {{end}}

sg_alert_rules.name: Low free space for storage pool

annotations.description: The space available for storing object data in the Storage Node is low.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to the ILM > Storage Pools page.
2. Select the storage pool listed in the alert, and select View Details.
3. Determine where additional storage capacity is required. You can either add Storage Nodes to each site in the storage pool or add storage volumes (LUNs) to one or more existing Storage Nodes.
4. Perform an expansion procedure. You can add new Storage Nodes or add storage volumes (LUNs) to existing Storage Nodes. See the instructions for expanding a StorageGRID system. If your grid is nearly full, see the instructions for planning a StorageGRID expansion.

sg_alert_rules.name: Storage Node not in desired storage state

annotations.description: The LDR service on a Storage Node cannot transition to the desired state because of an internal error or volume related issue
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Confirm that all volumes in the Storage Node are online (Nodes > Storage Node > Storage > Volumes).
2. If all volumes are online and this alert persists, contact support.

annotations.description: The space available for /var/local is low. If this condition is not addressed, S3 operations might fail.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to the Alerts page. Monitor this alert to see if the issue resolves on its own and the disk space becomes available again.
2. Contact technical support if the available space continues to decrease.
annotations.total: {{ with printf "node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance='%s', mountpoint='/var/local'}" $labels.instance | query }} {{ . | first | value }} {{end}}

annotations.description: The space available in the /tmp directory is low.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to the Alerts page. Monitor this alert to see if the issue resolves on its own and the disk space becomes available again.
2. Contact technical support if the available space continues to decrease.

sg_alert_rules.name: Expiration of server certificate for Management interface

annotations.description: The server certificate used for the management interface is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to Configuration > Certificates > Management interface certificate.
2. Select Use custom certificate to upload or generate a new certificate.

annotations.description: The amount of RAM available on a node is low.
annotations.recommendedActions:
Low available RAM could indicate a change in the workload or a memory leak with one or more nodes.

1. From the Grid Manager, go to the Alerts page. Monitor this alert to see if the issue resolves on its own.
2. If the available memory falls below the major alert threshold, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The amount of installed memory on a node is low.
annotations.recommendedActions: Increase the amount of RAM available to the virtual machine or Linux host. Check the threshold value for the major alert to determine the default minimum requirement for a StorageGRID node. See the installation instructions for your platform.

annotations.description: Errors have occurred while transferring data between nodes.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. If the "Grid Network MTU mismatch" alert is active, resolve that alert first. This alert might resolve when the MTU mismatch is fixed.
2. Other network connectivity errors might clear without manual intervention. If the issue persists, contact technical support.
annotations.networkTransmitErrors: {{ with printf `clamp_max(max without (device) (increase(node_network_transmit_errs_total{instance='%s'}[15m]) / increase(node_network_transmit_packets_total{instance='%s'}[15m])), 1)` $labels.instance $labels.instance | query }} {{ . | first | value }} {{end}}
annotations.networkReceiveErrors: {{ with printf `clamp_max(max without (device) (increase(node_network_receive_errs_total{instance='%s'}[15m]) / increase(node_network_receive_packets_total{instance='%s'}[15m])), 1)` $labels.instance $labels.instance | query }} {{ . | first | value }} {{end}}

annotations.description: A high percentage of the network frames received by a node had errors.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert might indicate a hardware issue, such as a bad cable or a failed transceiver on either end of the Ethernet connection.

  1. If you are using an appliance, try replacing each SFP+ or SFP28 transceiver and cable, one at a time, to see if the alert clears.
  2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: One or more network devices are down or disconnected.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert indicates that a network interface (eth) for a node installed on a virtual machine or Linux host is not accessible.
Contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: Node not in sync with NTP server

annotations.description: The node is not in sync with the network time protocol (NTP) server.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1.  Verify that you have specified at least four external NTP servers, each providing a Stratum 3 or better reference.
2.  Check that all NTP servers are operating normally.
3.  Verify the connections to the NTP servers. Make sure they are not blocked by a firewall.

sg_alert_rules.name: Node not locked with NTP server

annotations.description: The node is not locked to a network time protocol (NTP) server.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1.  Verify that you have specified at least four external NTP servers, each providing a Stratum 3 or better reference.
2.  Check that all NTP servers are operating normally.
3.  Verify the connections to the NTP servers. Make sure they are not blocked by a firewall.

annotations.description: The object existence check job has failed.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Select Maintenance > Object existence check.

2. Note the error message. Perform the appropriate corrective actions:

  Failed to start, Lost connection, Unknown error
  a. Ensure the Storage Nodes and volumes included in the job are online and available.

  b. Ensure there are no service or volume failures on the Storage Nodes. If a service is not running, start or
  restart the service. See the grid node maintenance procedures.

  c. Ensure the selected consistency control can be satisfied.

  d. After resolving any issues, select Retry. The job will resume from the last valid state.

  Critical storage error in volume
  a. Recover the failed volume. See the maintenance procedures for grid node recovery.

  b. Select Retry.

  c. After the job completes, create another job for the remaining volumes on the node to check for additional errors.

3. If you are unable to resolve the issues, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The object existence check job has stalled.
annotations.recommendedActions:
The object existence check job cannot continue. Either one or more Storage Nodes or volumes included in the job are offline or unresponsive, or the selected consistency control can no longer be satisfied because too many Storage Nodes are down or unavailable.

1. Ensure that all Storage Nodes and volumes being checked are online and available (select Nodes).
2. Ensure that sufficient Storage Nodes are online and available to allow the current coordinator node to read object metadata using the selected consistency control. If necessary, start or restart a service. See the grid node maintenance procedures.

   When you resolve steps 1 and 2, the job will automatically start where it left off.

3. If the selected consistency control cannot be satisfied, cancel the job and start another job using a lower consistency control.
4. If you are unable to resolve the issues, contact technical support.

annotations.description: Unexpected object size detected during object existence check procedure.
annotations.recommendedActions: Contact technical support.

annotations.description: Too few Storage Nodes with the RSM service are running or available at a site.
annotations.recommendedActions: Make sure that the majority of the Storage Nodes that have the RSM service at the affected site are running and in a non-error state.

annotations.description: One or more objects potentially lost from the grid.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert might require investigation to verify data wasn't lost and is still retrievable.

1. Investigate this alert immediately. You might need to take action to prevent further data loss. You also might be able to restore a lost object if you take prompt action. See "Lost and missing object data" in the instructions for troubleshooting StorageGRID.

2. When the underlying problem is resolved, reset the counter:

  a. On the Nodes page, select the grid, site, or Storage Node.

  b. Select Tasks.

  c. Under Reset Objects potentially lost counter, select Reset.

  The lost objects count is reset for the grid, site, or Storage Node, depending on your selection.

sg_alert_rules.name: Expiration of global server certificate for S3

annotations.description: The global server certificate for S3 is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to Configuration > Certificates > S3 API certificate.
2. Select Use custom certificate to upload or generate a new certificate.

annotations.description: A storage device cannot be accessed.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert indicates that a volume cannot be mounted or accessed because of a problem with an underlying storage device.

1. Check the status of all storage devices used for the node.

  a. If the node is installed on a virtual machine or Linux host, follow the instructions for your operating system to run hardware diagnostics or perform a filesystem check.

  b. If the node is a StorageGRID appliance model starting with SG1, SG6, SGE6, or SGF6 (examples: SG110, SG6060, SGF6112), use the BMC.

  c. If the node is a StorageGRID appliance model starting with SG5 (examples: SG5712, SG5860), use SANtricity System Manager.


2. If necessary, replace the component. For a StorageGRID appliance, see the maintenance procedures for your hardware.

annotations.description: A high percentage of quota space is being used. This rule is disabled by default because it might cause too many notifications.
annotations.recommendedActions:
If a tenant exceeds its quota, new ingests are rejected.
1. From the Grid Manager, select Tenants.
2. Sort the table by Quota Utilization.
3. Select a tenant whose quota utilization is close to 100%.
4. Do either or both of the following:

  a. Select Edit to increase the storage quota for the tenant.

  b. Notify the tenant that their quota utilization is high.

5. Repeat these steps for each tenant whose quota utilization is close to 100%.

annotations.description: When trace configuration is enabled, system performance might be negatively impacted.
annotations.recommendedActions: 1. Go to the Grid Manager > API Documentation > Go to private API documentation > traces. 2. Use GET /private/trace-config to determine the current trace configuration. 3. Use POST /private/trace-config/restore-default to restore the default trace configuration when traces are no longer required.

annotations.description: One or more services are unresponsive, or the node cannot be reached.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert indicates that a node is disconnected for an unknown reason. For example, a service on the node might be stopped, or the node might have lost its network connection because of a power failure or unexpected outage.

Monitor this alert to see if the issue resolves on its own. If the issue persists:
1. Determine if there is another alert affecting this node. This alert might be resolved when you resolve the other alert.
2. Confirm that all of the services on this node are running. If a service is stopped, try starting it. See the grid node maintenance procedures.
3. Ensure that the host for the node is powered on. If it is not, start the host.
Note: If more than one host is powered off, see the instructions for recovery and maintenance.
4. Determine if there is a network connectivity issue between this node and the Admin Node.
5. If you cannot resolve the alert, contact technical support.

expressions.major: floor((time() - storagegrid_private_unexpected_reboot_timestamp)/(60*60)) <= 24 OR floor((time() - avg_over_time(storagegrid_private_unexpected_reboot_timestamp[60m]))/(60*60)) <= 24 AND on (instance, job) (up == 0)

annotations.description: A node rebooted unexpectedly within the last 24 hours.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Monitor this alert. The alert will be cleared after 24 hours. However, if the node reboots unexpectedly again, this alert will be triggered again.
2. If you cannot resolve the alert, there might be a hardware failure. Contact technical support.

annotations.description: A file was found in replicated object storage that could not be identified as a replicated object.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1.  Determine if there are any issues with the underlying storage on a Storage Node. For example, run hardware diagnostics or perform a filesystem check.
2.  After resolving any storage issues, perform an object existence check to determine if replicated copies, as defined by your ILM policy, are missing. See the instructions for troubleshooting StorageGRID.
3.  Monitor this alert. The alert will clear after 24 hours, but will be triggered again if the issue has not been fixed.
4.  If you cannot resolve the alert, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: FabricPool bucket has unsupported bucket consistency setting

annotations.description: A FabricPool bucket uses the Available or Strong-site consistency level, which is not supported.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Sign in to the tenant account.
2. Select View buckets from the dashboard, or select STORAGE (S3) > Buckets.
3. Select the bucket name from the table.
4. From the Bucket options tab, select the Consistency level accordion.
5. Select "Read-after-new-write", which is the default consistency level.

sg_alert_rules.name: FabricPool bucket has unsupported versioning setting

annotations.description: A FabricPool bucket has versioning or S3 Object Lock enabled, which are not supported.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Sign in to the tenant account.
2. Select View buckets from the dashboard, or select STORAGE (S3) > Buckets.
3. Select the bucket name from the table.
4. From the Bucket options tab, select the S3 Object Lock accordion.
5. If S3 Object Lock is enabled, contact technical support for assistance.
6. Otherwise, expand the Object versioning accordion and select Suspend versioning.

annotations.description: The temperature of the compute controller in a StorageGRID appliance has exceeded a nominal threshold.

3. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

1. Check the hardware components for errors, and follow the recommended actions:

  a. If the appliance model starts with SG1, SG6, SGE6, or SGF6 (examples: SG110, SG6060, SGF6112), use the BMC.

annotations.description: A Fibre Channel link problem has been detected between the appliance storage controller and compute controller
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert might indicate that there is a problem with the connectivity between the storage and compute controllers in the appliance.

1. Check the hardware components for errors, and follow the recommended actions:

  a. Verify the fibre cables between controllers are completely connected.

  b. Ensure the fibre cables are free of excessive bends.

  c. Confirm that the SFP+ modules are properly seated.


2. If necessary, replace components. See the maintenance procedures for your hardware.
Note: If this problem persists, the problematic connection may be taken offline automatically.

annotations.description: The power of a StorageGRID appliance has deviated from the recommended operating voltage.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Check the status of power supplies A and B to determine which power supply is operating abnormally.

  a. If the appliance model starts with SG1, SG6, SGE6, or SGF6 (examples: SG110, SG6060, SGF6112), use the BMC.

  b. If the appliance model starts with SG5 (examples: SG5712, SG5860), use SANtricity System Manager.

2. If necessary, replace the component. See the maintenance procedures for your hardware.

annotations.description: There is a problem with one or more connections between the compute controller and storage controller.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to the appliance to check the port indicator lights.

2. If a port's lights are off, confirm the cable is properly connected. As needed, replace the cable.

3. Wait up to five minutes.
Note: If a second cable needs to be replaced, do not unplug it for at least 5 minutes. Otherwise, the root volume might become read-only, which requires a hardware restart.

4. From the Grid Manager, select Nodes. Then, select the Hardware tab of the node that had the problem. Verify that the alert condition has resolved.

annotations.description: One or more client certificates are about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to Configuration > Certificates.
2. Select the Client tab.
3. Select a certificate that will expire soon.
4. Select Attach new certificate to upload or generate a new certificate.
5. Repeat these steps for each certificate that will expire soon.

annotations.description: The MTU setting for the Grid Network interface (eth0) differs significantly across nodes in the grid.
annotations.recommendedActions:
The differences in MTU settings could indicate that some, but not all, networks are configured for jumbo frames. An MTU size mismatch of greater than 1000 might cause network performance problems.
1. To list the MTU settings for eth0 on all nodes, navigate to "https://<Primary Admin IP>/metrics/graph" and enter the following query:

   node_network_mtu_bytes{device='eth0'}


2. Modify the MTU settings as necessary to ensure they are the same for the Grid Network interface (eth0) on all nodes.

  * For appliance nodes, see the instructions for maintaining your appliance configuration.

  * For Linux- and VMware-based nodes, see the details about MTU in troubleshooting network, hardware, and platform issues.

annotations.description: The most recent AutoSupport message failed to send.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Review the settings on the Support > AutoSupport page. Check for failures on the Results tab.
2. Review "Troubleshoot AutoSupport messages" in the instructions for administering StorageGRID.
3. After updating any settings, select "Send User-Triggered AutoSupport" to send a test message.
4. If this alert persists, disable AutoSupport or contact technical support.
5. If a logs-based send has failed, go to the Logs page to retry the request.

annotations.description: One or more grid federation certificates are about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:

2. Select the connection whose certificate will expire soon.
3. Select Rotate certificate to generate new certificates for this connection.

annotations.description: One or more certificates in the admin proxy server CA bundle is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to Configuration > Proxy settings.
2. Select Admin.
3. Select Browse button to upload a new CA bundle.
3. Select Save.

2. Select an endpoint that has a certificate that will expire soon.
3. Select Edit endpoint to upload or generate a new certificate.
4. Repeat these steps for each endpoint that has an expired certificate or one that will expire soon.

expressions.major: sum by (connection_id) (increase(storagegrid_private_cgrscanner_emit_permanently_failed_requests[1d])) > 0 OR sum by (connection_id) (storagegrid_private_cgrscanner_emit_permanently_failed_requests UNLESS storagegrid_private_cgrscanner_emit_permanently_failed_requests offset 1d) > 0

annotations.description: A cross-grid replication error occurred that requires user intervention to resolve.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to Configuration > System > Grid federation, and locate the connection name listed in the alert.
2. On the Permitted tenants tab, look at the Last error column to determine which tenant accounts have errors.
3. To learn more about the failure, go to Support > Tools > Metrics and select "Cross Grid Replication" under Grafana.
4. For help troubleshooting this alert, go to "Troubleshoot grid federation errors" in the instructions for administering StorageGRID.
Note: After you resolve the issue, it might take up to 1 day for the alert to clear. To confirm that the issue is resolved, review the cross-grid replication metrics or go to the Last error column for the affected tenant, and select Clear error. Then, ingest new objects into the bucket and confirm that the error does not reappear.

annotations.description: Cross-grid replication requests are pending because a resource is unavailable.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Monitor this alert to see if the issue resolves on its own.
2. If the issue persists, determine if there is a "Grid federation connection failure alert" for either grid in the connection or an "Unable to communicate with node alert" for any node. This alert might be resolved when you resolve those alerts.
3. To learn more about the failure, go to Support > Tools > Metrics and select "Cross Grid Replication" under Grafana.
4. If there are no other alerts, go to "Troubleshoot grid federation errors" in the instructions for administering StorageGRID.
5. If you cannot resolve the alert, contact technical support.

3. If this port is disconnected on purpose, disable this rule. From the Grid Manager, select Alerts > Alert Rules, select the rule, and click Edit rule. Then, uncheck the Enabled check box.

annotations.description: Very slow disk I/O might be impacting grid performance.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Examine the storage system that hosts this node's volumes to determine and correct the root cause of the slow I/O.

  * If the issue is related to an appliance Storage Node that has SANtricity System Manager, check for faulty drives, drives with predicted faults, or in-progress drive repairs.
    Also check the status of the links between the appliance compute and storage controllers to see if any links are down or showing excessive error rates.
    See "Configure SANtricity System Manager" in the documentation for StorageGRID appliances.

  * Otherwise, examine the base operating system or hypervisor that hosts the node. Identify and correct any issues.

2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.
Note: Affected nodes might disable services and reboot themselves to avoid impacting overall grid performance. When the underlying condition is cleared and these nodes detect normal I/O performance, they will return to full service automatically.

annotations.description: A port on a StorageGRID appliance is not participating in the LACP bond.
annotations.recommendedActions: Check the configuration for the switch. Ensure the interface is configured in the correct link aggregation group.

annotations.description: Communication with the baseboard management controller (BMC) has been lost.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Confirm that the BMC is operating normally. Go to the Nodes > Hardware tab for the appliance node. Locate the Compute Controller BMC IP field, and browse to that IP.
2. Attempt to restore BMC communications by placing the node into maintenance mode and then powering the appliance off and back on. See the maintenance configuration procedures for your appliance.
3. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: Appliance Fibre Channel HBA port failure

annotations.description: A Fibre Channel HBA port is failing or has failed.
annotations.recommendedActions: Contact technical support.

annotations.description: The client certificate for an external syslog server is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to Configuration > Audit and syslog server.
2. Select Edit external syslog server.
3. Select Browse to upload the new certificate.
4. Select Browse to upload the new private key.
5. Complete the Configuration wizard to save the new certificate and key.

annotations.description: The certificate authority (CA) certificate used to sign the external syslog server certificate is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Update the CA certificate on the external syslog server.
2. Obtain a copy of the updated CA certificate.
2. From the Grid Manager, go to Configuration > Audit and syslog server.
3. Select Edit external syslog server.
4. Select Browse to upload the new certificate.
5. Complete the Configuration wizard to save the new certificate and key.

annotations.description: The server certificate presented by the external syslog server is about to expire.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Update the server certificate on the external syslog server.
2. If you previously used the Grid Manager API to provide a server certificate for
   certificate validation, upload the updated server certificate using the API.

annotations.description: Node cannot forward logs to the external syslog server.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to Configuration > Audit and syslog server.
2. Select Edit external syslog server.
3. Advance through the Configuration wizard until you are able to select Send test messages.
4. Select Send test messages to determine why logs cannot be forwarded to the external syslog server.
5. Resolve any reported issues.

2. Select Edit external syslog server.
3. Advance through the Configuration wizard until you are able to select Send test messages.
4. Select Send test messages to determine why logs cannot be forwarded to the external syslog server.
5. Resolve any reported issues.

sg_alert_rules.name: Audit logs are being added to the in-memory queue

annotations.description: Node cannot send logs to the local syslog server and the in-memory queue is filling up.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Ensure that the rsyslog service is running on the node.
2. If necessary, restart the rsyslog service on the node using the command 'service rsyslog restart'
3. If the rsyslog service cannot be restarted and you do not save audit messages on Admin Nodes, contact
   technical support. Audit logs will be lost if this condition is not corrected.

annotations.description: A problem with a fan unit in the appliance was detected.
annotations.recommendedActions:
Caution: If a fan problem persists, the appliance might reach unacceptable operating temperatures.
1. Inspect the fan unit for loose power connections or obstructions. Resolve any issues you find.
2. If necessary, replace the fan unit. See the maintenance instructions for your appliance.

annotations.description: A problem with a network interface card (NIC) in the appliance was detected.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Reseat the NIC. Refer to the maintenance instructions for your appliance.
2. If necessary, replace the NIC. See the maintenance instructions for your appliance.

annotations.description: A problem was detected with a direct-attached storage (DAS) drive in the appliance.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Ensure the drive is correctly installed and connected. Refer to the installation instructions for your appliance.
2. If necessary, replace the drive. See the maintenance procedures for your hardware.

sg_alert_rules.name: Appliance DAS drive is in the wrong slot or node

annotations.description: A direct-attached storage (DAS) drive is in the wrong slot or node
annotations.recommendedActions:
Physically move the drive to the expected slot in the expected node.
If you are certain that no drives are installed in the wrong slots or nodes, the system might be detecting old formatting. Contact technical support to resolve this condition.

annotations.description: A direct-attached storage (DAS) drive is rebuilding. This is expected if it was recently replaced or removed/reinserted.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Determine the reason that caused the drive to rebuild.
2. Optionally, silence this alert while the drive is being rebuilt. Rebuilding might take hours or days, depending on the drive size.
3. If necessary, replace the drive. See the maintenance procedures for your hardware.

annotations.description: The security policy doesn't require FIPS mode, but FIPS modules are in use.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to Maintenance > Rolling reboot.
2. To disable the use of FIPS modules, reboot the node listed in this alert. This alert will clear after the node is rebooted.
3. If this alert persists after the node has been rebooted, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The security policy requires FIPS mode, but FIPS modules aren't in use.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to Maintenance > Rolling reboot.
2. To enable the use of FIPS modules, reboot the node listed in this alert. This alert will clear after the node is rebooted.
3. If this alert persists after the node has been rebooted, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The configuration of the nginx service is invalid. The previous configuration is now being used.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. See error details in /var/local/log/nginx/config-generation.log.
2. If TLS and SSH policy changes were made recently, go to Configuration > Security settings.
3. On the TLS and SSH policies tab, select "Use policy" for any non-custom policy.
4. If the alert is still not resolved, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The configuration of the nginx-gw service is invalid. The previous configuration is now being used.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. See error details in /var/local/log/nginx/config-generation.log.
2. If TLS and SSH policy changes were made recently, go to Configuration > Security settings.
3. On the TLS and SSH policies tab, select "Use policy" for any non-custom policy.
4. If the alert is still not resolved, contact technical support.

annotations.description: The configuration of the SSH service is invalid. The previous configuration is now being used.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. See error details in /var/local/log/ssh-config-generation.log.
2. Go to Configuration > Security settings.
3. On the TLS and SSH policies tab, select "Use policy" for any non-custom policy.
4. If a custom policy is invalid, go to the Grid Manager > API Documentation > Go to private API documentation > ciphers > /grid/ciphers for more details on how to correct it.
5. If the alert is still not resolved, contact technical support.

annotations.description: A storage volume is offline and needs attention.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Resolve other storage-related alerts that might have caused this alert.
2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: Storage volume needs to be restored

annotations.description: A storage volume has been recovered and needs to be restored.
annotations.recommendedActions:
Important: If the node might contain the only copy of an object, do not perform these steps. Contact technical support to determine if data can be restored.
1. From the Grid Manager, go to Maintenance > Volume restoration.
2. Select the node that contains the affected volume from the "Nodes to restore" tab and start restoration. Then, wait for the restoration to complete.
3. If Volume restoration mode is Automatic and this alert remains after a long time, see "Manually restore failed volume or node" in the documentation.
4. If this alert persists after all node volumes are restored, contact technical support.

annotations.description: A storage volume has been offline for more than 5 minutes.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. If the "Storage volume needs attention" alert is also active for the same volume, follow the recommended actions for that alert. Resolving the "Storage volume needs attention" alert should resolve this alert.
2. If the "Storage volume needs attention" alert is not active, repeat the steps to mount and format storage volumes, as described in the StorageGRID maintenance or expansion instructions.
3. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: S3 PUT object size too large

annotations.description: A client is attempting a PUT Object operation that exceeds S3 size limits.
annotations.recommendedActions: See "Troubleshoot the S3 PUT Object size too large alert" in the documentation for troubleshooting a StorageGRID system.

sg_alert_rules.name: Volume Restoration failed to start replicated data repair

annotations.description: Replicated data repair for a repaired volume couldn't be started automatically.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Resolve other storage-related alerts that might have caused this alert.
2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: An appliance SSD is reporting a critical warning.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Locate the warning index value or values for the alert.
2. For each index value listed, complete the corrective action, as follows:

  Warning index 0: Available spare space capacity has fallen below threshold. Replace the drive.

  Warning index 1: Temperature is out of range. Check for other temperature-related alerts and correct any issues found.

  Warning index 2: NVM subsystem degraded.  Replace the drive.

  Warning index 3: Media has been placed in read-only mode. Check for other warnings and alerts and correct any issues found.

  Warning index 4: Volatile memory backup device has failed. Replace the drive.

  Warning index 5: Persistent memory region has become read-only or unreliable. Check for other warnings and alerts and correct any issues found.

3. If other index values appear or if this alert persists after you perform the corrective actions, contact technical support.

expressions.major: (storagegrid_appliance_support_cru_failure{"type"="FANS"} == 1 or on(instance, tray) storagegrid_appliance_fan_failure == 1) or ((avg_over_time(storagegrid_appliance_support_cru_failure{"type"="FANS"}[60m]) >= 0.9 or on(instance, tray) avg_over_time(storagegrid_appliance_fan_failure[60m]) >= 0.9) AND on (instance, job) (up == 0))

annotations.description: A problem with a fan unit in the storage controller for an appliance was detected.
annotations.recommendedActions:
Caution: If a fan problem persists, the appliance storage controller might reach unacceptable operating temperatures.
1. Inspect the fan unit for loose power connections or obstructions. Resolve any issues you find.
2. If necessary, replace the fan unit. See the maintenance instructions for your appliance.

sg_alert_rules.name: Appliance DAS drive locator light on

annotations.description: The drive locator light for one or more direct-attached storage (DAS) drives in an appliance Storage Node is on.
annotations.recommendedActions:
Follow these steps to see which locator lights are on and to turn off any lights you are no longer using.

1. Go to the Nodes page.
2. Select the Storage Node and then select Manage drives.
3. On the Layout tab, look for the light bulb icon to determine which drive has its locator light on.
4. Select the drive.
5. Select Turn locator light off.

sg_alert_rules.name: Appliance DAS drive exceeding limit for data written per day

annotations.description: An excessive amount of data is being written to a drive each day, which might void its warranty.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert is triggered if the number of bytes written to a drive per day would cause the Total Bytes Written (TBW) limit to be reached before the end of the warranty.

Determine why the drive is receiving a large amount of data each day. Review any recent changes that might increase the load on the appliance Storage Node. For example, did you activate a new ILM policy? Are you using a new erasure-coding profile? Have you added new S3 clients?

For more details on SSD warranty endurance, go to Support > Tools > Metrics and select "SSD Warranty" under Grafana.

If this is an expected burst that will not continue indefinitely, you can ignore this alert.

annotations.description: An appliance has not been booted securely.
annotations.recommendedActions: This appliance must use UEFI secure boot. Contact technical support.

annotations.description: The number of TCP connections on this node is approaching the maximum number that can be tracked.
annotations.recommendedActions:
To avoid reaching the limit, which will prevent new connections from being established and might impact inter-node communications and cause operations to fail:
1. Reduce the number of active connections to this node.
2. Reduce the rate of new connections to this node.
3. Reduce the rate of aborted client operations.
4. Contact technical support if this issue persists.

annotations.description: The receive usage on the Admin Network is high.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Review the node_network_receive_bytes_total metric for all interfaces on the node to understand how traffic is currently distributed among Grid, Admin, and Client Networks.
2. If you expect this condition and do not want to receive future alerts, edit the rule and unselect the Enabled check box (must have the Manage Alerts permission).
3. If the node is an appliance, consider using the Grid and Client Networks for more traffic. Review network types and bond modes for network configuration options.

annotations.description: The transmit usage on the Admin Network is high.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Review the node_network_transmit_bytes_total metric for all interfaces on the node to understand how traffic is currently distributed among Grid, Admin, and Client Networks.
2. If you expect this condition and do not want to receive future alerts, edit the rule and unselect the Enabled check box (must have the Manage Alerts permission).
3. If the node is an appliance, consider using the Grid and Client Networks for more traffic. Review network types and bond modes for network configuration options.

sg_alert_rules.name: Platform Services pending request capacity low

annotations.description: The number of Platform Services pending requests is approaching capacity.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert is triggered if the number of persisted Platform Services requests is reaching capacity. A large number of pending requests might mean that one or more of the Platform Services endpoints are misconfigured. If capacity is reached, new client requests configured to use Platform Services will fail.
To view which tenants have a large number of persisted Platform Services requests, log in to an ADC Storage Node (ssh admin@grid_node_IP), switch to root (su -), and enter 'rsmtool accounts'. The output will contain a list of tenants, each one having an attribute 'ActiveRequests', which denotes the number of pending requests for that tenant.
When you have identified the tenant with the large number of pending requests, look at that tenant's Platform Services endpoints page in the Tenant Manager to investigate the Platform Services request errors.

annotations.description: Errors sending SNMP inform notifications to a trap destination.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Go to Configuration > Monitoring > SNMP Agent.

2. Under Trap destinations, confirm that the following trap destination values are correct:
   * Version
   * Host
   * Protocol
   * Port
   * Community (SNMPv1 or SNMPv2c-only)
   * USM user (SNMPv3-only, also confirm USM user is correctly configured at the management station)

3. Check for the type of error in /var/local/log/sg-snmp-agent.log. A "connect refused" error indicates
   that the SNMP trap receiver is not running. A timeout error indicates that the trap destination host
   could not be reached or that the community string or USM user were not recognized.

annotations.description: SSH external access has been enabled for more than 24 hours.
annotations.recommendedActions:
* If external SSH access shouldn't be enabled, disable it.
* If external SSH access is intentionally enabled for the long term, you can disable this alert rule.

annotations.description: In the past 24 hours, a user has logged in with Web Console or SSH.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Verify this activity was authorized.
2. If this action was not initiated by a recognized administrator, secure the system immediately.

annotations.description: A problem was detected with the boot device in the appliance.
annotations.recommendedActions: Contact technical support.

annotations.description: A problem was detected with the CMOS battery in the appliance.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Replace the CMOS battery. See the maintenance procedures for your hardware.

2. If this alert persists, contact technical support.

annotations.description: An elevated percentage of connections to load balancer endpoints disconnected without performing requests.
annotations.recommendedActions:
This alert indicates unusual client activity, and bandwidth on your load balancer endpoints might be reduced for legitimate clients and can cause Gateway and Admin Nodes to become unresponsive.
1. Confirm if your grid is receiving an elevated number of requests to one or all of your load balancer endpoints from a broad range of clients or IP addresses.
2. Refer to the zero-request diagnostics on the Grid Manager Diagnostics page to determine the duration of the unusual client activity.
3. If the increase in network traffic is not expected, collect network logs and work with technical support to determine which ports are being targeted.

annotations.description: A storage volume was offline and triggered an automatic remount. This could indicate a drive issue or filesystem errors.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. Resolve other storage-related alerts that might have caused this alert.
2. Determine how often the volumes required remounting, and if the volumes successfully remounted:

  * Examine the /var/local/log/miscd.log file for error information.

  * Check appliance details in the Grid Manager for drive status. Select NODES > Storage and NODES > Manage drives.

  * Check the Grafana Node dashboard to determine if the appliance is receiving fewer reads and writes, which could indicate a drive is consistently going offline because it's starting to fail.

3. If the alert was triggered during a drive replacement, recheck the alert status after 24 hours.
4. If this alert persists after 24 hours, or the volumes did not remount, contact technical support.

sg_alert_rules.name: Log archival destination bucket not found

annotations.description: The log archival destination bucket is missing, which prevents logs from being archived to the destination bucket.
annotations.recommendedActions:
1. From the Grid Manager, go to Configuration > Monitoring > Log management.
2. Select "Log location", then "Use a bucket".
3. Select "Change tenant and bucket".
